result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens returning the raw `fetch` Response in sync mode (`const response = await fetch(...); return response;`), while hubspot's CalendarService assigns its result directly to `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. A fetch Response lacks access_token/refresh_token fields, so the mechanism described is verifiable in the diff and constitutes a real type-safety/correctness defect.

judged_text: In sync mode the value awaited into `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` is a raw fetch Response, and a fetch Response has none of the HubspotToken fields (access token / refresh token) that the subsequent code reads and persists into credential.key. Each sync-mode hubspot refresh writes a credential key whose token fields are undefined, permanently breaking the hubspot integration for affected users until manual reconnection.

Each sync-mode hubspot refresh writes a credential key whose token fields are undefined, permanently breaking the hubspot integration for affected users until manual reconnection.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` is assigned the awaited return of `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. In sync mode that value will be a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken` (no `access_token`/`refresh_token` fields), so any subsequent code that reads token fields from `hubspotRefreshToken` will break at runtime and/or persist invalid data.
